findings.conclusion: E2 is the lowest-token online path under both backbones, but it trades away semantic quality.
For Qwen, E5 gives the highest Strict and Soft scores, but it is the most expensive store and query path.
For DeepSeek selective retrieval, E7 reaches the joint-best Strict score at far lower query-token cost than E1 or E5, although E1 retains slightly higher Soft and F1.
Full Context has the highest DeepSeek-family Strict and Soft scores, but only by one Strict-correct question and with lower F1 than several selective systems.

S2 construction is modest and E3 crosses E1 after 46 Qwen or 35 DeepSeek queries. S3-backed E6/E7 can amortise only against the expensive E1 path after 187--324 repeated queries; they never become token-saving alternatives to E2, and E5 has no token break-even.
Observed recovery overhead is concentrated in R1 conditions; 39 of 41 failed attempts account for 10.13 million additional tokens, while two DNS failures have unknown usage.
More retrieval work is not automatically better: RQ5 attributes more confirmed internal failures to Answerer utilisation than to retrieval.

rq6_direct_answer: No single condition is best under every objective. E2 is the lowest-token path; E3 is the strongest Qwen balance after its modest S2 build is amortised; E5 is the Qwen semantic-quality maximum at very high cost; E7 is the strongest DeepSeek selective query-time compromise when S3 is already available; E1 remains the no-build auditable quality baseline; and Full Context is a diagnostic semantic-quality fallback rather than a universal replacement for retrieval.

unavailable_claims.complete_recovery_token_ranking: Recovery usage is isolated and reported separately for 39 of 41 attempts; two DNS failures have unknown token usage
